skill.name: system-integration-validator
skill.description: Validates integration readiness before deployment by guiding checks for ports, databases, API contracts, blocked workflows, and data-flow dependency issues.
skill.summary: Guides pre-deployment integration checks for services, APIs, and workflow data flow.
skill.author: BarisSozen

security_audit.summary: The static shell, fetch, /dev/null, and port-check hits are documentation examples for local diagnostics, so they were marked false positives. The bundled audit_report.json contains self-issued safety verdicts that could influence reviewers or agents and should not ship with the skill. No credential exfiltration, destructive commands, or hidden external endpoints were found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Remove audit_report.json from the published skill package, or strip risk_level, safe_to_publish, and similar verdict fields from distributed content.

remediation.issue: Diagnostic command examples can be mistaken for automatic execution
remediation.suggestion: Label shell snippets as optional local diagnostics and state that users should approve commands before running them.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The bundled audit_report.json asserts "risk_level": "safe" and "safe_to_publish": true. Embedded safety verdicts can pressure later reviewers or agents to trust the author-provided assessment instead of the active audit.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The safety claims are explicit in audit_report.json, but they are structured report fields rather than direct override instructions. That makes the injection risk plausible but less certain than an imperative prompt.

content.value_statement: Integration drift can block deployments and create late failures. This skill guides checks for ports, databases, API contracts, and data flow before release.
actual_capabilities: Lists pre-deployment checks for ports, databases, API contracts, and data flow.
Provides local port-check examples for common service ports.
Shows PostgreSQL and Redis readiness checks.
Highlights API contract mismatches between frontend calls and backend endpoints.
Identifies dead ends, orphan inputs, bottlenecks, and circular dependencies in workflows.
limitations: Provides guidance and example checks; command execution depends on the host tool and user approval.
Focuses on common local services like PostgreSQL, Redis, and web ports.
Requires accurate endpoint and workflow information from the user.
Does not replace full automated integration tests or observability.

use_cases.title: Check Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Validate local service ports, database readiness, and API assumptions before staging or production deployment.

use_cases.title: Debug Blocked Workflows
use_cases.description: Trace dead ends, orphan inputs, bottlenecks, and circular dependencies when backend workflows stop progressing.

use_cases.title: Align Frontend And Backend APIs
use_cases.description: Compare frontend requests with backend endpoints to find contract mismatches before release testing.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Port Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned local services and tell me which ports I should verify before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Database Readiness Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me validate PostgreSQL and Redis readiness for my local environment. Include connection, migration, and timeout checks.

prompt_templates.title: API Contract Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare frontend calls and backend endpoints
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this frontend and backend API description. Identify route, method, payload, status, and timeout mismatches.

prompt_templates.title: End-To-End Flow Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this system workflow for dead ends, orphan inputs, bottlenecks, circular dependencies, and deployment blockers.

output_examples.input: Validate my web app before deployment.
output: Ports: Review the web, API, database, cache, and admin ports before starting services.
Databases: Confirm PostgreSQL and Redis are reachable and ready for application traffic.
APIs: Compare frontend calls with backend routes, methods, payloads, and response expectations.
Data flow: Check for orphan inputs, dead ends, bottlenecks, and circular dependencies.

output_examples.input: My checkout workflow hangs after payment authorization.
output: Trace each step from payment authorization to order creation and notification.
Look for an output that no downstream service consumes.
Verify that timeout handling exists for external calls.
Check whether retry logic can create a circular dependency.

output_examples.input: Review my frontend and backend API plan.
output: Match each frontend request to one backend route.
Compare method, path, required fields, response shape, and error handling.
Flag missing timeouts and unclear retry behavior.
Create a short release checklist from any gaps found.

best_practices: Confirm ports before starting services or running deployment scripts.
Test database readiness with connection, permission, migration, and simple query checks.
Review API contracts and data flow after changing endpoints or workflow steps.
anti_patterns: Running deployment checks only after a release has failed.
Assuming a reachable database means migrations and permissions are valid.
Ignoring circular dependencies when workflows hang.

faq.question: What does this skill validate?
faq.answer: It guides checks for ports, database readiness, API contracts, and workflow data flow before deployment.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Execution depends on the AI tool, environment, and user approval.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide service ports, database types, endpoint descriptions, workflow steps, and known deployment symptoms.

faq.question: Can this replace integration tests?
faq.answer: No. Use it to prepare and review checks, then run automated integration tests for proof.

faq.question: Does the skill send data externally?
faq.answer: The skill files do not define an external collection endpoint. They include local diagnostics and timeout examples.
